expectations.text: Recommends splitting the class by responsibility (does NOT endorse keeping all 4 concerns in one file)
expectations.evidence: 'Short answer: no, I'd split this one'; 'Split by responsibility' into auth/tokens.ts, users/profile-repository.ts, notifications/user-emails.ts, analytics/user-events.ts plus thin orchestrator.

expectations.text: Identifies the seams (auth / persistence / email / analytics) as genuinely independent and isolatable
expectations.evidence: 'four things that happen to touch a User... Each can be understood, and edited, with almost no reference to the others' — lists token, profile CRUD, email, analytics each 'Self-contained.'

expectations.text: Cites the ~300-line ceiling AND/OR multiple-unrelated-concerns as the reason, not blind line count
expectations.evidence: 'Past roughly 300 lines, and once a file spans several concerns, signal-to-noise is the dominant problem — and you've cleared both thresholds.'

expectations.text: Pushes back on the 'keep everything in one place for the agent' rationale as misapplied to a god object
expectations.evidence: 'The thing you're optimising for — Claude having full context — is exactly what this file undermines'; 'Your heuristic is sound; it's just mismatched to this file. UserService isn't one cohesive thing.'
